children: Bank of America Securities this week introduced a 2027 year-end S&P 500 (
) target of 7,800, contending that a recent market pullback has created an attractive entry point despite looming earnings deceleration and supply-demand headwinds.

The forecast implies roughly 8.6% upside from Wednesday’s close of 7,182.86—and about 7% from Friday’s implied futures open of 7,290.94—with BofA’s underlying models mapping a wider potential range between 6,600 and 8,500. The index's all-time intraday high is 7,844.52, set in October.

Strategists remain constructive on the back of compressed price-to-earnings multiples and untapped AI-driven productivity gains, noting that higher capital costs and regulatory hurdles should prevent an AI capital expenditure overheat. Reflecting greater value for existing AI
to Overweight while highlighting stronger conviction in AI adoption through Overweight ratings on financials

Still, BofA projects S&P 500 earnings-per-share growth to slow sharply from 35% ($370) in 2026 to 14% ($420) in 2027—modestly below the $428 consensus—before normalizing to 7% ($450) in 2028. Because chipmakers

drive the bulk of profit growth, a 20% cut in AI spending could directly shave 8% off index EPS, compounding broader downside risks from rising equity issuance, waning share buybacks, and potential demographic-driven retirement outflows.

title: BofA sets 2027 S&P 500 target at 7,800 after pullback
